evals.prompt: How do I set up FCM push notifications in Flutter from scratch? I need to handle foreground, background, and when the app is terminated.
assertions: Response covers all three app states: foreground (onForegroundMessage stream + local notification), background (top-level @pragma('vm:entry-point') handler registered via FirebaseMessaging.onBackgroundMessage), and terminated (getInitialMessage() on startup)

Response uses the Strategy / Clean Architecture pattern: PushMessage entity in domain, FcmPushProvider in data layer, NotificationBloc in presentation — no direct firebase_messaging imports outside the data layer
Response includes the required Firebase initialization in main() before runApp, and the background handler must be a top-level function that calls configureDependencies() independently

evals.prompt: My NotificationBloc needs to navigate to a specific screen when the user taps a notification. How do I handle deep link navigation from push messages?
assertions: Response listens to onMessageOpenedApp stream (background tap) AND calls getInitialMessage() at startup (terminated tap) inside NotificationBloc or an InitializePushUseCase

Response extracts the route/deep-link from PushMessage.data and delegates navigation without importing go_router or Navigator directly into the BLoC — navigation is triggered via a BLoC state that the UI layer consumes
Response distinguishes the two tap scenarios: background tap uses onMessageOpenedApp stream, terminated tap uses getInitialMessage() in the initialization flow

evals.prompt: ¿Cómo manejo el token de FCM y lo envío al servidor cuando se actualiza? El token puede cambiar después de que el usuario reinstala la app.
assertions: La respuesta cubre tanto la obtención inicial del token (getToken()) como la escucha de actualizaciones (FirebaseMessaging.instance.onTokenRefresh stream) dentro del FcmPushProvider o el repositorio
La respuesta indica que el token debe enviarse al servidor propio cada vez que cambie (no solo en el primer login), e incluye un ejemplo de GetPushTokenUseCase o equivalente en la capa de dominio
La respuesta está en español (idioma del prompt) y menciona que el token puede invalidarse por reinstalación de la app, restauración de backup o rotación de claves FCM

evals.prompt: I want to be able to switch from FCM to OneSignal without rewriting my BLoC or domain layer. How?
assertions: Response explains the Strategy pattern: PushProvider abstract interface in the data layer with FcmPushProvider and OneSignalPushProvider as concrete implementations — the BLoC and all domain use cases depend only on PushNotificationRepository, never on FCM or OneSignal directly
Response shows how the active provider is selected at build time via --dart-define=PUSH_PROVIDER=fcm or PUSH_PROVIDER=onesignal, resolved in PushProviderModule with GetIt/Injectable
Response confirms that swapping providers requires zero changes in domain or presentation layers — only pubspec.yaml dependencies and the dart-define flag change

evals.prompt: How do I test my NotificationBloc in unit tests without needing a real FCM connection?
assertions: Response mocks PushNotificationRepository (the domain interface) using Mocktail — NOT FcmPushProvider or FirebaseMessaging directly, keeping tests provider-agnostic
Response uses bloc_test with a fake stream for onForegroundMessage and onMessageOpenedApp to verify state transitions without any real Firebase dependency
Response explicitly states that background top-level handlers (@pragma vm:entry-point) should NOT be unit-tested directly — test the UseCases they delegate to (e.g., ProcessBackgroundMessageUseCase)

evals.prompt: How do I request notification permission from the user?
assertions: Response addresses the FCM/messaging side within this skill: FirebaseMessaging.instance.requestPermission() (iOS) and POST_NOTIFICATIONS Android manifest entry (Android 13+), or the equivalent in PushNotificationRepository.requestPermission()
Response explicitly scopes the OS-level permission request flow (permission_handler, PermissionService, point-of-use UX patterns, rationale dialogs) to the flutter-permissions skill, not this skill
Response does not conflate the two concerns: this skill owns the FCM/push infrastructure and token lifecycle; flutter-permissions owns the OS permission dialog orchestration and status handling
